data.narrative:
The Nuclear Company is a Series A-stage nuclear energy developer that has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 11 firms across the nuclear sector—3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Oklo. The peer set spans seed through Series B stages, providing both forward and backward reference points.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised of $50M as a proxy for current value, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage advancement, implying a $100M valuation. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A)—yields a median of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The wide dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity and varying commercial maturity within the nuclear technology landscape.

Triangulation of these two methods produces a valuation range of $85M to $929M, with a median of $454M. The stage-progression floor of $85M–$100M reflects conservative early-stage positioning, while the peer-median result of $808M anchors the upper bound. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to the Fuse Energy comparable, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital intensity of commercialization in the nuclear sector.
